body:
In just their second season of existence, the Golden State Valkyries are WNBA champions

        The Golden State Valkyries are the WNBA champions. In just their second year of existence, the Valkyries battled the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA Finals and emerged victorious on Saturday night with a 68-63 decision in a thrilling Game 7. Golden State was led by a historic performance from Gabby Williams, who scored 28 of her 30 points in the second half to lead the Valkyries to a come-from-behind win. The Valkyries had the chance to close the series out in Atlanta in Game 6, but the Dream, propelled by their home crowd, forced the first Game 7 in WNBA history. It lived up to the hype to close out a historic season, the WNBA's 30th. To reach this stage, the Dream and Valkyries both completed semifinal sweeps. Atlanta knocked out the New York Liberty, while Golden State ousted the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces. The Dream knocked the Washington Mystics out in the first round and are a perfect 5-0 in the playoffs. The Valkyries defeated the Dallas Wings in the first round, needing all three games to do so. The Finals, for the second season ever, are a best-of-seven series in 2026.The 2026 WNBA season has been groundbreaking, on and off the court. It launched on the heels of a contentious and extended labor battle that resulted in a historic raise for the players (the salary cap increased from $1.5 million in 2025 to $7 million in 2026), and in return, the players raised the bar on a weekly basis. Multiple regular-season records fell this year, from Clark becoming the first player in WNBA history with a 40-point, 10-assist game, to Angel Reese breaking the single-game rebounding record with 26 to Kelsey Mitchell passing A'ja Wilson's single-season points record.2026 WNBA playoff bracket

        Only two matchdays remain in the Apertura portion of the Liga MX season as everyone is chasing Club America, who are first on 28 points with a game in hand still to play. With the most goals scored in the league, America are back to their best, but that will also make their match against fifth-place Toluca an interesting one. Toluca are the reigning champions, but, due to a mixture of injuries and bad luck, have seen the squad slip from where they'd expect to be.They're healthy now, so it'll be a great chance for them to show that they're still among the contenders as the playoffs loom, but they aren't the only side in need of that. Monterrey are currently in a playoff position by the skin of their teeth despite the spending that brought Hugo Cuypers and Diego Rossi to the club; the attack has only been a mid-table effort, while the defense has also struggled. Monterrey are one of the most successful clubs in Liga MX history, so missing the playoffs would be a shock, but it's also a very real possibility as they face Club Tijuana.Tijuana have struggled while teenage phenom Gilberto Mora has been out with an injury, but this is a very winnable game for the club and one that could push them as high as fifth depending on how things shake out. title: Borussia Dortmund spoil Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or coronation, keep pace in Bundesliga title race - CBS Sports
description: Fabio Silva scored in the dying minutes of the game to ensure Dortmund would come out with a 2-2 draw at Bayern M
body:
Fabio Silva scored in the dying minutes of the game to ensure Dortmund would come out with a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MUNICH – Few things are as straightforward as handing the ball to a Ballon d'Or-winning striker from the penalty spot. So when Harry Kane stepped up in the 56th minute at the Allianz Arena, there was little reason to expect anything other than a goal on a day that seemed tailor-made for him. Before kickoff, Bayern Munich had turned Der Klassiker into a celebration of Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph. Accompanied by his family, Kane walked onto the pitch carrying the trophy as Bayern unveiled a giant banner bearing his likeness in the center circle and flag-bearers waved red-and-white Bayern flags around the pitch. The striker even wore a special red jersey with gold trim befitting the game's newest golden boy. Yet five days after collecting soccer's most prestigious individual award, Kane drove his penalty against the crossbar, the ball ricocheting back into play rather than over the line.The miss was not a deterrent for Bayern, who went on to unleash 23 shots worth 4.05 expected goals to Borussia Dortmund's 12 and 0.63. The numbers reflected their status as the Bundesliga's undeniable heavyweight, pinning Dortmund back for long stretches as the Allianz Arena swelled with every attack and groaned with every near miss. For once, though, life came at Bayern fast. Kane's penalty was merely the first sign that this would not be a routine Der Klassiker. A 2-2 draw followed, ensuring the title race would survive another weekend and leaving the two sides level on points, just as they had entered the night.
By the numbers, Bayern had done enough to win and may have left feeling aggrieved by the crossbar's intervention. It denied Kane from the spot and, deep into stoppage time, thwarted Lennart Karl's curling effort from the edge of the box. Yet the hosts never fully established the relentless rhythm that has become their hallmark. Bayern generated chances in waves, but Dortmund repeatedly found moments to slow the tempo, relieve pressure and remind their rivals that control of the match was never quite as complete as control of the shot chart. The match ebbed and flowed, each team enjoying meaningful stretches of possession, creating a tension that lingered until the final whistle.To Dortmund's credit, they identified the only realistic way to blunt Bayern's superiority. The visitors did not stop Bayern from attacking, a near-impossible task these days. Instead, they prevented the match from becoming the avalanche Bayern so often creates. The hosts managed 15 touches in Dortmund's penalty area through the opening 37 minutes, a figure consistent with their season norms, but they needed more time and more passes to get there. Dortmund shared possession almost evenly for the first half hour, slowing Bayern's tempo and holding them to 284 touches in that span, well below their Bundesliga average of 344.9.The quality of Bayern's chances lacked their usual verve until Konrad Laimer's 38th-minute strike turbocharged an attack that has rarely missed a beat, even without Luis Diaz (hamstring). Kane's penalty proved to be the match's inflection point, though, a moment that revealed the competing realities at the heart of the draw. Bayern saw a match they largely controlled but failed to put away. Dortmund saw proof that resilience, rather than dominance, might be enough to keep pace.
"I probably could have been out there for another hour today and the ball wouldn't have gone in the back of the net," Kane said afterward. "You have to take that on the chin sometimes ... It's nothing to cry about."Kane's response reflected Bayern's outlook. They left frustrated but hardly concerned, armed with enough evidence to believe the performance mattered more than the scoreline.For Dortmund, the miss felt like a reprieve. Der Klassiker has often become an exercise in surviving Bayern's pressure, and for a moment it looked as though the visitors were about to confront a two-goal deficit. Instead, Kane's effort rattled the crossbar and gave Dortmund belief -- something that was increasingly valuable as the match wore on.
"Harry is such a great penalty taker," Dortmund goalkeeper Gregor Kobel said. "You can't really predict it, but I just tried to [not] give him anything. The last time I tried to fake him out a little bit, but then the timing for me was a little bit bad in the last game. Today, I thought I'd just give him nothing. I tried to make it hard as soon as possible for him and luckily it worked."
Belief, not control, became Dortmund's currency. Bayern continued to create chances and monopolize threatening territory, but the visitors gradually turned the match into the sort of uneven, uncomfortable contest they needed.Serhou Guirassy was a likely candidate for Dortmund's equalizer, while Dayot Upamecano joined Laimer on Bayern's scoresheet in the 66th minute. For another 22 minutes, it felt like the hosts were inching closer to their preferred outcome -- Kane and Michael Olise may not have been the clear standouts on Saturday, but Bayern's squad is constructed well enough that other players can handle the slack. If the night was supposed to belong to Kane, it ultimately created room for an unlikely headliner. That role fell to Dortmund's Fabio Silva.
The Portuguese forward is not among the first names on Dortmund's team sheet, but he is steadily developing a reputation as one of Niko Kovac's most dependable options. His goal against Bayern was his fourth in all competitions this season, already eclipsing last season's total despite spending much of the campaign in a reserve role. Though his goals have attracted attention, Silva's seven assists last season serve as a reminder that his value extends well beyond finishing chances."Every game is important for me," he said. "It's not about scoring against Bayern. I'm just thinking of helping the team with my football. Not all about goals. I remember two or three actions before the goal, I was there to help the team to create some chances. I think I'm as a player more than [just about] scor[ing] goals … Of course, I prefer [to] start than be on the bench. If I say the opposite, I'm not going to be 100% honest with you, but I always try to be positive during the week when I see I don't play. Of course, the first moment I'm angry, but after, I try to always be positive because I know I can be important for the team."Dortmund will continue to face questions about whether they can truly match Bayern over the course of the season. Saturday night did little to erase them. The shot totals, expected goals and overall flow of the game all pointed toward Bayern's superiority. Yet title races are not decided by underlying numbers alone. On a day built to celebrate Kane's coronation, Dortmund left Munich with something nearly as valuable -- proof that Bayern can be frustrated, and that the race remains alive.

title: Lakers drama: Jeanie Buss accuses siblings of conspiring against her in court filing - CBS Sports
description: Buss accused her siblings of a 'cloak and dagger' campaign through the media in a court filing this week
body:
Buss accused her siblings of a 'cloak and dagger' campaign through the media in a court filing this week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:55 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Jeanie Buss has accused her siblings of conspiring against her in a "cloak and dagger" campaign through the media in a court filing this week and has asked a judge to block her siblings' attempts to sell the family's shares of the Los Angeles Lakers, ESPN reports.According to Wednesday's filing, Jeanie Buss said her siblings -- specifically Joey and Jesse Buss -- are jealous of their father's decision to leave her with governor rights to the team and she does not want them selling the family's remaining shares of the team.Finality for both sides of the legal spat could come during a scheduled Dec. 8 hearing in Los Angeles Superior Court.Former Disney CEO Bob Iger and Josh Kushner spearhead an ownership group looking to buy the Lakers from Mark Walter at a valuation of $12.5 billion. 

        
            
                Jeanie Buss disputes her family's sale of Lakers stake: What to know about dramatic off-court fight
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"The conflicts that ensued after Dr. (Jerry) Buss's death (in 2013) were sadly inevitable, and no doubt intensified given that Dr. Buss chose his daughter over four sons to be his successor," representation for Jeanie Buss wrote in this week's filing. "Respondents' obsession with tearing down Jeanie and their inability to accept that she would be a part of the Lakers' future is borne of this classic succession parable."Jeanie Buss would no longer serve as the Lakers' governor if her family sells its 17.8% ownership stake, which is just above the NBA's 15% minimum for the family to retain control. Iger previously said during an interview with The California Post that the plan was for Buss to remain governor, but "if things change, they'll change." The latest filing continues an ongoing saga between family members over the NBA's third-most valuable franchise. Earlier this year, ESPN reported that Jeanie Buss contended that a 2017 court order prevents any vote to sell the remaining family shares without her consent. 
That was not the first time that the Buss siblings have fought over control of the team. When Jeanie fired Jim Buss as head of basketball operations in 2017, he and Johnny Buss attempted to strip Jeanie of her seat on the Lakers' board of directors. The two sides ultimately agreed to settle with Jeanie Buss remaining in control of the team.Now, Jeanie Buss is asking the court to remove two siblings as co-trustees of the trust for breach of fiduciary duty, hold them in contempt of court, and "find Jim, Johnny and Jesse liable for aiding and abetting a violation of the 2017 court order and be reimbursed for legal costs," per ESPN.
If the Buss family sells the entirety of its shares of the team, each sibling receives an additional $371 million per go-along rights. ESPN reported this week that settlement talks have begun."Jeanie had no choice but to seek court intervention to enforce the clear terms of the trust and this court's 2017 order," Wednesday's filing states. "Respondents respond (by) casting themselves as victims, when in reality, the entire episode is their own false flag operation."The cloak and dagger, backroom 'votes' and 'resolutions' shared with ESPN, rather than their co-trustee and sister, and subsequent refusal to discuss the matter, was intended to force Jeanie's hand, cry victim and again smear her in the media by sharing in advance their specious response."

title: Georgia escaped Florida, but passing-game concerns threaten title hopes - CBS Sports
description: Georgia's defense and ground game have masked issues through the air, but tougher opponents could force the Bulld
body:
Georgia's defense and ground game have masked issues through the air, but tougher opponents could force the Bulldogs to open things up
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:57 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Coming out of its bye week, No. 3 Georgia began its home stretch with a big 27-8 win over No. 17 Florida. You never snub your nose at a three-score rivalry win, but the Bulldogs' offensive performance wasn't as rosy as the scoreboard might suggest.Georgia totaled just 318 yards of offense against a Florida defense that has been leaky all season, but, to be fair, some of that was due to the defense. The Bulldogs forced four turnovers. One of them resulted in a scoop-and-score, and two more resulted in short fields, which Georgia converted into 10 points.The biggest question about the Dawgs' offense after this win is the passing game. The running game eventually found some consistency, allowing Georgia to lean on the Gators in the second half. Quarterback Gunner Stockton, on the other hand, couldn't find much success against one of the worst secondaries in the conference.Entering the game, Florida ranked 13th in the SEC and 121st nationally in passing yards allowed per game (255.0). The Gators also ranked 112th in EPA per dropback (0.23) and 126th in passing success rate (50.7%).
Despite that, Stockton finished the game with just 101 passing yards on 13-of-23 passing. Freshman Craig Dandridge was the team's leading receiver with 39 yards, and 32 of those yards came on the Bulldogs' longest pass play of the game.In his postgame interview with ESPN's Holly Rowe, Kirby Smart complimented Stockton's grit and willingness to run the ball but admitted that Georgia has to get better through the air."We missed some throws," Smart said. "We left some points out there. We gotta get better."
He's not wrong. If Georgia wants to achieve its goal of winning the national championship, Stockton and his pass-catchers will have to be much better than they were today, and that day may come sooner rather than later.Big tests coming for BulldogsOver the next three weeks, Georgia will face quarterbacks capable of scoring points, even against one of the best defenses in the conference.Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss are stepping into the batter's box, Austin Simmons and Missouri are on deck, and LaNorris Sellers and South Carolina are in the hole.
There's a good chance at least one of those quarterbacks forces Georgia to engage in a higher-scoring game. If that happens, are the Bulldogs capable of answering the bell?Stockton has turned in some big games this season. He threw for 295 yards and three touchdowns against Vanderbilt, and he made some incredibly difficult throws in Georgia's road win over Alabama. Still, the lack of production against Florida is a red flag.For starters, even when some of the production is there, Stockton has been prone to mistakes. Just look at the Bulldogs' loss to Auburn. He played well for 90% of the game, but his three turnovers played a key role in the Tigers leaving Athens with a win.
It doesn't help that Georgia hasn't had any playmakers emerge in the receiving game. Dandrige is the team's leading receiver with 20 receptions for 349 yards. The Bulldogs are loaded at tight end, but none of those players have become real threats in the passing game on a consistent basis. Lawson Luckie leads that group with 12 catches for 197 yards and two touchdowns.Maybe the Bulldogs can get through the regular season by patching together their passing attack. After all, the defense is capable of holding talented quarterbacks in check. We've already seen that with Keelon Russell. Who's to say that unit can't give Chambliss, Simmons and Sellers problems too?But Georgia's ultimate goal isn't to go 11-1 in the regular season. It isn't even to win the SEC Championship. The Bulldogs have their sights set on a national championship, and they will likely encounter potent offenses along the way. Miami, Notre Dame, and LSU are all capable of putting crooked numbers on the scoreboard. Ohio State has the best player in the country, with Jeremiah Smith putting up monster numbers every week.
At some point, Georgia will need its passing attack to make big plays, and it's fair to wonder whether that will happen when the moment arrives.

title: Steelers vs. Browns: Rivals battle in Week 8 with first place in AFC North on the line - CBS Sports
description: Plus, where to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert
body:
Plus, where to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        One of the NFL's greatest rivalries is alive and well. On Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns will duel with first place in the AFC North on the line. Both teams enter Sunday's game with 5-2 records. The Browns, by virtue of their Week 4 win over Pittsburgh, are technically the division leader. Cleveland responded to a loss to the Jets in Week 5 with wins over Baltimore and Tennessee. Pittsburgh has won three straight since losing to Cleveland. Last Sunday, the Steelers became the first team to win a game in Paris after recording a 16-10 win over the Saints. Here's how you can follow the action, along with a breakdown and a prediction. Where to watch Steelers vs. Browns liveWhen: Sunday, Nov. 1 | Time: 1 p.m. ETWhere: Acrisure Stadium -- Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow:  CBS Sports AppOdds: Steelers -3.5, O/U 39.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook)Steelers vs. Browns: Need to know Last time we met: The Browns' 27-24 win over Pittsburgh in Week 4 was their fifth consecutive win over the Steelers in Cleveland. The Browns led 21-7 before withstanding Pittsburgh's comeback attempt. The Steelers' comeback was spearheaded by Aaron Rodgers, who threw two fourth-quarter touchdown passes. 
The Steelers tied the score with 1:42 left, but four completions by Deshaun Watson on Cleveland's ensuing drive set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining. Rodgers threw for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions in a losing effort. Jaylen Warren ran for 93 yards on 17 carries, and DK Metcalf led Pittsburgh's receivers with 115 yards on five catches. Cleveland's offense ran through rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who combined to catch nine passes for 153 yards. 
Steelers are finding their groove on both sides of the ball: Pittsburgh's three-game winning streak is largely the byproduct of better play from the offensive line and a defense that is continuously improving. Pittsburgh's offensive line surrendered five sacks of Rodgers back in Week 4. Rodgers has been sacked nine times in the three games since. While that's still not great, it is a sign of the unit's continuous improvement.The line has also helped revive the Steelers' rushing attack, which has improved further with Rico Dowdle's return. The duo specifically made their presence felt during Pittsburgh's game-winning drive in overtime in Tampa Bay back in Week 6. 
Defensively, the Steelers have made marked improvements since the loss in Cleveland, which was the Steelers' first game after Joey Porter Jr. was traded to Dallas. The unit is currently fifth in the NFL in points allowed, fourth in touchdown passes allowed, sixth in average yards per carry allowed, seventh in third-down efficiency and eighth in red zone efficiency. Linebacker Payton Wilson has been one of the Steelers' defensive standouts during the winning streak. He made a key interception during last week's win over the Saints. Browns offense ready to take off? While Cleveland's defense has been solid all year, its offense has at times left something to be desired. They are coming off their best performance in recent moments, however. 
Against the Titans, the Browns piled up 491 yards while receiving excellent balance. They threw for 308 yards and ran for 183. Cleveland did turn the ball over twice after not doing so a week earlier in a 13-10 win over the Ravens. Really, the big question in Cleveland is whether or not Watson can beat an elite defense. He'll try to show that he can on Sunday. Prediction The Steelers have two distinct advantages. They have the better quarterback and a running game that should be able to take advantage of a Browns defense that is 22nd in the NFL in average yards-per-carry allowed. If Dowdle and Warren get going, that should help open things up for Rodgers and the passing game. Score: Steelers 20, Browns 16

title: Oklahoma offense stuck in neutral: Loss to South Carolina highlights key decisions ahead for Brent Venables - CBS Sports
description: Saturday's loss to South Carolina as a home favorite marked another disappointing outing for the John Mateer-Ben
body:
Saturday's loss to South Carolina as a home favorite marked another disappointing outing for the John Mateer-Ben Arbuckle pairing before a fourth-quarter flurry
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oklahoma coach Brent Venables faces tough decisions at season's end about how to manage his offense, particularly the need for an identity under coordinator Ben Arbuckle, whose unit continues to hamper the Sooners' progress this fall.Saturday's boo-filled 42-25 loss to South Carolina was another data point in a campaign marked by offensive struggles, including ineptitude at home against Kentucky, a spanking at Georgia, and a near whiff against New Mexico in Week 3 that magnified lingering issues from last fall.Since upending top-ranked Texas in Red River to begin October, Oklahoma's offensive production has reverted to its anemic norm, and the Sooners are now 4-4 overall, 2-3 in the SEC. They're only one game over .500 in conference play under Venables (20-19) and are in danger of their third losing season in five years without a strong finish.Can Venables and Arbuckle find a way to get out of this funk before the end of the season and offer momentum entering 2027?
It's complicated.Without any semblance of a rushing attack early against the Gamecocks, quarterback John Mateer completed 7 of 12 passes in the first half of Saturday's loss for 25 yards, most of those throws being quick tosses to the perimeter and none to the second level. The Sooners had more penalty yards than offensive yards by intermission and trailed 28-10, Oklahoma's lone score coming on an interception return for a touchdown from Kip Lewis in the second quarter. Venables came off the field harping on lack of execution and explosive plays, a similar song and dance to what's been said previously. Venables hired Arbuckle after the 2024 season to reinvigorate the program offensively, and he brought Mateer with him from Washington State to run the show, but the Sooners' ROI has waned with the pairing.Yes, Oklahoma appeared in the College Football Playoff last season, but did so in spite of inconsistencies offensively anchored by a stingy defense. Down the stretch last November, the Sooners had 47 offensive possessions over four games before the CFP's first round, with 25 finishing in punts, five resulting in turnovers and one ending on downs. 
Nine finished with a successful field goal and seven ended in touchdowns. And of those touchdown possessions, only two spanned five or more plays. History has repeated itself this fall. Oklahoma entered Saturday's Week 9 game at the bottom of the SEC in total offense, rushing offense and 15th in scoring offense — all statistics that are worse than last season's showing.According to TruMedia, coming into Saturday's game, Oklahoma's three-and-out rate this season was 34.1%, which ranked 120th nationally."It ain't changing," Oklahoma grad and analyst Dari Nowkah said at halftime from the SEC Network set. "You'll see No. 10 trot back out there. That's been the story every game of John Mateer's career; there are opportunities, they're just not being discovered."
Will changes happen at Oklahoma?The Sooners scored 13 points during a loss two weeks ago to Kentucky, stalled a couple times inside the red zone leading to field goals during a 23-15 win at Mississippi State in Week 8 and didn't find their rhythm against the Gamecocks until it was too late and against second-team defenders.Oklahoma scored three points over its first eight offensive possessions before a fourth-quarter flurry included a pair of touchdown passes from Mateer to Ivan Carreon, his first scores of the season. Mateer finished 26-of-43 passing for 244 yards, much of that total coming in garbage time with the outcome sealed an hour earlier.Unless the Sooners hit a grand slam this transfer portal cycle with one of the best-available quarterbacks for 2027, Oklahoma will enter the offseason in a few weeks with two true freshmen, senior Whitt Newbauer and sophomore Bowe Bentley among others. Newbauer and Bentley have combined for two passing attempts this season, and it'll be impossible for Venables to sell Oklahoma's fanbase on another offseason of offensive patience.
Arbuckle is finishing up the second season of a three-year deal as play-caller, and while his scheme has provided windows for success, execution has faltered. The Sooners must determine who they want to be on offense, identifying that identity and implementing it as part of the fabric of the program.Right now, the Sooners are struggling to manufacture advantages for Mateer, who hasn't had help in the backfield.Venables knows what championship defense looks like. He coached plenty of them at Clemson and had one last fall with the Sooners. Venables is responsible for figuring this out and gelling with an offensive coordinator who doesn't put the onus on Oklahoma's defense every weekend.
Running this back in 2027 and expecting a surge offensively isn't going to work, unless Oklahoma lands a quarterback who can execute what's called or Arbuckle takes an identity first mindset into the offseason and hammers it home with the players.

        No. 4 Indiana will host Minnesota on Saturday afternoon on CBS (3:30 p.m. ET), as the Hoosiers try to calm the nerves of fans in Bloomington who have grown antsy watching an offense struggling to get going. While the Hoosiers remain ranked inside the top five, there's plenty of anxiety in Indiana about an offense that's been sputtering with just 48 points combined in the last three games. A 13-6 win in overtime against a listless Michigan team didn't assuage those concerns, and now they welcome a Minnesota team that has proven to be a thorny opponent. The Gophers come in at 5-2 fresh off a 13-10 win over Iowa to hoist the Floyd of Rosedale trophy, as PJ Fleck is 2-for-2 in rivalry games this season. Minnesota will need to step up their level in the next two games against top-10 foes in Indiana and UCLA, but if the Hoosiers get caught looking ahead to a trip to USC, they can quickly find themselves in a dogfight with the Gophers despite being 20.5-point favorites. Will the Hoosiers' offense come to life back at home and re-establish themselves as one of the nation's elite? Can Minnesota pull off another stunner by dragging Indiana into the mud? We'll find out on Saturday afternoon in what could be another thrilling, tense Big Ten battle. 
Where to watch Minnesota vs. Indiana liveDate: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ETLocation: Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, IndianaTV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports AppStreaming on Paramount+ Premium  Minnesota vs. Indiana: Need to know  Hoosiers need more from Hoover: Indiana's still a top 5 team, but this is clearly not a squad at the same level as last year. That's largely due to an offense stuck in the mud, with a quarterback who has not clicked with the scheme despite two highly talented receivers on the outside. 
Josh Hoover has been dreadful the last few weeks, and when the Hoosiers have won, it's been in spite of their quarterback's play. That might not need to change to win this week specifically, but the Hoosiers are desperate to establish some form of offensive rhythm in the back half of the season before the College Football Playoff. The Gophers present challenges, but this is the caliber of team Indiana should be able to handle with ease. They've not proven to have that gear so far this season, and it's incumbent on Hoover to be both more dynamic and more efficient throwing the football for them to find that next level. DE-FENSE [clapclapclap]: The defenses for both teams are their point of strength, and both teams will be looking to their defensive playmakers to help them out. The Hoosiers and Gophers put forward defensive masterclasses in low-scoring wins a week ago, but Minnesota is the team with the greater questions on that side of the ball. 
There have been games where Minnesota looks fantastic defensively (like last week against Iowa), but they have struggled against teams that can stretch the field and have high-level athletes on the outside. Indiana has that in Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh, but the question is whether Josh Hoover can get them the ball on time and on target regularly enough to take advantage of their mismatches. Indiana has no such questions, and they'll start by trying to take away Minnesota's ground game and dare Drake Lindsey to beat them through the air. Can Drake Lindsey protect the football? There's a world where the Gophers hang around in this one and are a live dog on the road to pull a stunning upset. However, that only happens if Lindsey protects the football, something he's not excelled at this season. Lindsey leads the Big Ten with six interceptions and has thrown at least one in each of Minnesota's last five games. 
The Gophers have to maximize every possession to have a chance against Indiana, and given the Hoosiers have an elite defense, there won't be any room for error on Lindsey's part. He came into the season with NFL Draft buzz because of his physical tools, but he's got to manage risk better in the second half of the season to boost that stock. Saturday will be his biggest test yet on the road.   Minnesota vs. Indiana prediction, picks  If it ain't broke, don't fix it. The Hoosiers are quite simply an under machine right now. It's not just that they have an elite defense and a sputtering offense, but it's the way Curt Cignetti is managing games. The lack of trust in Hoover is never more apparent than when he trots the punt unit out on a fourth-and-short at midfield without hesitation. Even if Indiana dominates, it's hard to see them piling up points on a good Minnesota defense, and there's a real world where the Gophers keep this close throughout. Either way, it'll come down to the team that converts opportunities into touchdowns rather than field goals, and this total is a bit too high at 40. Pick: UNDER 41.5

        Every lineup decision matters as the Fantasy football season approaches its midpoint, and Week 8 presents another challenging slate for managers trying to separate dependable starters from potential disappointments. With four teams on bye, injuries continuing to shake up depth charts and several big-name players facing difficult matchups, knowing who to trust could be the difference between securing a much-needed victory and watching valuable Fantasy points pile up on your bench.      That's where Dave Richard's Week 8 PPR cheat sheet comes in. Jahmyr Gibbs, Puka Nacua and Bucky Irving enter the week as some of the most trustworthy Fantasy options, while Quinshon Judkins faces a difficult matchup against Pittsburgh and Denver's crowded backfield presents another headache for managers. Whether you're choosing between established stars or searching for an overlooked flex option, Dave's confidence scores can help you navigate those difficult start/sit decisions and build the strongest possible lineup.      What do the numbers mean? All weekly analysis, from data points to matchup outlooks to game-flow predictions, is represented as a number on a 1-10 confidence scale. The higher the number next to a player's name, the more confident I am that you should start him. The numbers are not projections but confidence scores to help you pick who to start. All relevant players for this week are listed, so if you do not see a player's name, do not start him.                  
To find a specific player, use your search function (CTRL-F on PCs and Command-F on Macs). If neither is an option, or if you're on a mobile device, you can search by typing the name in the URL bar or scrolling down by game. If you're still unsure, just send Dave a note (@DaveRichard), and he will take a look, time permitting. Remember to use the #AskFFT hashtag!         Saul "Canelo" Alvarez returns to the ring for the first time in more than a year on Saturday when he faces WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli in Saudi Arabia. Alvarez will be fighting for the first time since dropping his undisputed super middleweight championship to Terence Crawford in September 2025.Mbilli was promoted from interim to full champion by the WBC in the wake of Crawford's retirement after dominating Alvarez. Despite being promoted rather than winning the belt in the ring, Mbilli is a world-class fighter. He brings a relentless power-punching style to the ring and will look to overwhelm arguably the greatest fighter of the generation in Alvarez.Be sure to keep up with all the action on Saturday with our live coverage of Alvarez vs. Mbilli, including round-by-round scoring and updated fight results throughout the night!For Alvarez, even a rare fight where he is not the man entering the ring as champion feels like another day at the office. That's a product of Alvarez being a staple of pound-for-pound lists and championship fights for nearly two decades. While some believe that Alvarez's loss to Crawford was the product of time and ring miles catching up to him, Alvarez will look to use Saturday to show that he still has plenty left in the tank.
"I don't believe in shortcuts. I'm going straight for the champion because I already have the experience," Alvarez said at the final press conference. "I've been a champion for many years and I want to be a champion again."

title: Thomas Castellanos' performance in win over Arizona raises ceiling for Texas Tech - CBS Sports
description: Joey McGuire's bold switch at quarterback unlocked a dormant rushing attack, giving the Red Raiders a dual-threat
body:
Joey McGuire's bold switch at quarterback unlocked a dormant rushing attack, giving the Red Raiders a dual-threat dimension that re-establishes them as Big 12 title contenders
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the waning moments of No. 13 Texas Tech's game against No. 22 Arizona, the Red Raiders faced a critical opportunity to put the game away. First-time starting quarterback Thomas Castellanos took a carry for only a few yards on second down, pulling down the linebackers and setting up third-and-one. The Red Raiders lined up in a two-back set, seemingly setting up another quarterback run. Castellanos set the ball in the mesh point for a read while the defense collapsed. Instead of pulling, running back J'Koby Williams clutched the ball, took one cut right and broke off a dramatic 64-yard run to put the finishing touches on a dramatic 34-26 win to wrestle control of the Big 12 back. Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire made a bold move, benching quarterback Will Hammond in favor of the journeyman Castellanos. But after finding their offense in the second half, Castellanos unlocks a new ceiling for the Red Raiders heading into the home stretch. 
Castellanos was a late addition to the Texas Tech roster after receiving an injunction, primarily rostered to give the Red Raiders some experienced depth behind first-year starting quarterback Will Hammond. But several weeks into Hammond's starting tenure, results were poor. Despite playing a relatively light schedule, the Red Raiders ranked bottom half in the Big 12 in total offense under Hammond's watch. The running game, especially, was lackluster as defenses stacked the box and challenged an inconsistent offensive line. Hammond threw six touchdowns to six interceptions in his starts. While Castellanos is less of a factor in the passing game, the threat of his rushing is a game-changer for the Red Raiders. Seven of his carries went for first downs, and he broke off a pair of carries for 20-yard gains. Castellanos became the first Texas Tech quarterback to record 100 yards rushing since Tyler Shough. 
Castellanos threw for 144 yards and two touchdowns and added 117 yards and a score on the ground. But beyond the rushing production, defenses are forced to account for all 11 players. The switch made a huge difference for running back J'Koby Williams, who exploded for 175 yards and a touchdown in the win. The 328 yards rushing was the most surrendered by an Arizona defense since 2020, a 0-5 pandemic season under Kevin Sumlin. Since a 28-17 loss to BYU, the Wildcats have been on a tear. They won their last three games by an average of 28.0 points per game and rattled off a five-game winning streak. It was a prime opportunity for the Wildcats to knock off the reigning champs, coming off of a frustrating loss. Instead, Arizona gave up 34 points, the most since Sept. 27, 2025, against No. 14 Iowa State. 
To be clear, Castellanos has plenty of his own issues. The senior completed only 5 of 15 passes in the first half and 11 of 24 for the game, even below his career average of 58.5% completion. His passing is primarily a wrinkle on a run-based offense. Furthermore, Castellanos is still playing on a temporary injunction. Earlier this season, Castellanos briefly lost eligibility after a previous injunction was dissolved. Texas Tech can't be 100% confident that their new quarterback will stay eligible through the end of the season. Despite the drawbacks, Castellanos gives Texas Tech a much-needed spark heading into the home stretch of the season. With the 30-game starter in the lineup, the Red Raiders seriously re-enter the Big 12 race.

title: College football winners, losers: Dylan Raiola bounces back, Wisconsin falls flat - CBS Sports
description: Indiana escapes on a miracle field goal and Wisconsin gets blanked by Iowa as the early slate delivers chaos acro
body:
Indiana escapes on a miracle field goal and Wisconsin gets blanked by Iowa as the early slate delivers chaos across the top 25
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:51 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Week 9 college football slate looked like a lighter one, but there are always surprises to be found. Five AP Top 25 teams dropped in the first two windows of the day, including three to unranked opponents. Of course, No. 3 Georgia continues to flex its muscles, eviscerating rival Florida. No. 4 Indiana, though, needed some late heroics from its kicker. No. 13 Texas Tech finally looked the part of a Big 12 contender, while No. 25 Wisconsin's season slid to a screeching halt. In the night slate, USC hopes to pull off an upset against No. 2 Ohio State, and North Carolina challenges No. 1 Miami. Here are the biggest winners and losers of Week 9 heading into the primetime slate. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Indiana coach Curt CignettiHow does he keep getting away with it? No. 4 Indiana was dead to rights after Minnesota drilled a 60-yard field goal in the waning seconds of regulation. Cignetti appeared to completely mismanage the clock, letting 40 seconds run instead of taking a timeout. 
Then, Indiana miraculously nailed a 60-yard field goal of their own and produced the game-winning play to open overtime in a 23-16 victory against the Golden Gophers. Indiana is clearly diminished from its national title team, but it doesn't matter. Cignetti just, somehow, manages to find a way. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: WisconsinThe vibes were exceedingly positive in Madison after an impressive few performances to get Wisconsin back into the AP Top 25 under coach Luke Fickell. All the goodwill was spent in an instant as the Badgers lost a 30-0 stunner against Iowa. Wisconsin was completely outclassed on both sides of the ball, mustering only 52 yards rushing. They allowed Iowa quarterback Hank Brown to complete 20-of-24 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns, one of the best quarterback performances in years for the Hawkeyes. 
All the momentum from a breakout 2026 season is gone for the Badgers. Closing the year out with four unranked victories to reach nine wins would be nice, but below the expectations of this team after last week's domination of No. 16 USC. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Texas TechObituaries were started for Texas Tech's season after a stunning two-touchdown loss to Cincinnati last week. Instead of panicking, coach Joey McGuire handed the keys to backup quarterback Thomas Castellanos. The Red Raiders have now outdueled No. 22 Houston and No. 22 Arizona in impressive home performances, launching them into the Big 12 title discussion. With road trips to No. 24 Oklahoma State and Baylor remaining, the Red Raiders have a few more prove-it spots against two of the hottest teams in the conference. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: QB Dylan Raiola, OregonThe Raiola era at Oregon has been a mess ever since he was forced into the starting lineup in place of Dante Moore. After going down 10-0 against No. 20 Northwestern, it looked like the Ducks were heading towards another disastrous performance. After the early adversity, Raiola rose to the occasion. The Nebraska transfer completed 22-of-31 passes for 336 yards and three touchdowns in one of the best games of his career. New offensive coordinator Jay Johnson did a much better job of letting Oregon's star-studded receivers make moves in space. Oregon's playoff hopes are likely doomed, but a road trip against No. 2 Ohio State next week makes things awfully interesting. It's a major spot for Raiola to cement himself as a repaired prospect. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: OklahomaThe Sooners just keep finding new lows as Brent Venables heads towards his third losing season in five years. This time, it was a stunning 42-25 loss to South Carolina at home in a game that likely spelled the end of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle. For the first time this season, the Sooners' defense completely collapsed. The Sooners allowed 28 points in the first half alone and looked outmatched. There were multiple coverage busts, including an 84-yard breakaway for a touchdown from LaNorris Sellers to DJ Black. At this point, Oklahoma under Venables is bad at everything. The Sooners scored 15 points in garbage time to make the score look respectable, but this was a collapse. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: QB DJ Lagway, BaylorFor the second year in a row, DJ Lagway saw his coach fired. But under interim Baylor coach Joe Klanderman, Lagway played perhaps the best game of his career. Facing one of the stingiest defenses in the Big 12 in UCF, Lagway set back and picked them apart. He threw for 319 yards and four touchdowns without an interception, completing 64% of his passes in a 41-9 victory. It could just be a simple dead cat bounce, but Baylor played with more urgency than it has seen in years. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: SMUWith only one close loss on their record, No. 19 SMU looked like a potential spoiler in the College Football Playoff race. The Mustangs were a solid No. 3, within striking distance of Wake Forest and Miami. But after a stunning 30-27 loss against Syracuse, it's another frustrating season of what-ifs. 
The Mustangs have been painfully close the past several years to returning to the College Football Playoff, including a loss to California on the last play of the game. This was similarly painful, giving up a passing touchdown with 17 seconds remaining to a team that entered at 3-4 and searching for any consistency. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Sacramento StateThe Hornets had a brutal transition to FBS, losing their first seven FBS games by an average of 27.5 points per game. But finally, against Kent State, the Hornets recorded their first-ever FBS victory, 31-10. Running back Isaiah Ene rushed for 107 yards and two touchdowns in the win, and the Hornets can build some confidence as the season heads into the home stretch.
